answer: Give every identity a memory it cannot outsource. At registration a key commits to a salt, and each epoch it must echo back a digest of its own prior submissions, derived locally from that salt. A clone farm can copy a key once but cannot reproduce its whole history of derived state, so copies desynchronise and get caught. Add an onyx rule — one identity per distinct attested hardware root — and a gale of simultaneous signups collapses to the number of real machines.
